name: AVR ISP 6-pin (SPI programming)
description: The standard 6-pin in-system programming header for AVR microcontrollers (ATmega, ATtiny) and Arduino ICSP. It exposes the SPI lines plus RESET, so a programmer can clock firmware in while the chip is on the board. Pin 1 (MISO) is marked, often with a dot or a bevel on the shroud.

contacts.name: MISO
contacts.description: master-in slave-out (data from target to programmer)

contacts.name: VCC
contacts.description: target supply sense / power (do NOT back-power a running board unless intended)

contacts.name: MOSI
contacts.description: master-out slave-in (data from programmer to target)

variants: The older 10-pin AVR ISP has the same signals spread over 2x5 with extra grounds; a 10-to-6 adapter is common.
Arduino calls this the ICSP header; it is the same 6-pin AVR ISP pinout (MISO at pin 1).
gotchas: Pin 1 is MISO. Getting the header rotated 180 degrees is the #1 mistake -- always find the pin-1 marker (dot / square pad / shroud key).
Pin 2 (VCC) is target-power sense. Whether the programmer powers the target or the target must be self-powered depends on the programmer/jumper -- back-powering a board already on USB can conflict.

This is NOT UART/serial bootloader programming -- it drives the chip's SPI+RESET directly (works even with no bootloader), which is how you burn a bootloader or recover a bricked fuse... except an RSTDISBL or wrong-clock fuse still needs high-voltage programming, not ISP.
notes: Standard 6-pin AVR ISP / Arduino ICSP pinout (MISO/VCC/SCK/MOSI/RESET/GND). Universal across AVR toolchains.
